name: The Gregory
headline: The Gregory is a 165-unit, all-affordable new-construction apartment building for adults 55 and older (all at 60% AMI) on Plaza Drive in Highlands Ranch, developed by Shea Properties, which won a 2026 Federal 4% housing tax credit award financed with Douglas County Housing Partnership bonds.
why_it_matters: It is a straight 4% bond deal on private land in unincorporated Douglas County. It needed no rezoning (multifamily is a use by right in Highlands Ranch Planning Area 79). Douglas County's local bond cap, pooled at DCHP, carried the bonds. A metro-district park on part of the lot is the community give-back: a repeatable template for suburban senior LIHTC.

status.label: Credits awarded and bonds approved; construction start not confirmed
status.detail: The County approved the plat on 2026-03-10, and county staff reports list a 165-unit site improvement plan (SP2026-027) in process. The Board approved DCHP's bonds (up to $37M) on 2026-09-22. Shea's stated target was to start construction in Q4 2026 (November) and open in 2028. There is no public record of a bond closing, building permit or groundbreaking.

next_step: Watch for the County's approval of site improvement plan SP2026-027 and a building permit, and for DCHP's Multifamily Housing Revenue Bonds (The Gregory Project) to close, which would mark financial closing.

key_numbers.meaning: All 165 units are set at 60% AMI: 120 one-bedrooms and 45 two-bedrooms.
About $32.1M over the 10-year credit period (calculated). CHFA marks the amount subject to change.
CHFA's bond figure. The County's public approval allows up to $37,000,000.

key_numbers.value: 9.69-acre lot, about 1 acre to a metro-district park
key_numbers.meaning: Shea is building a community park on the lot that will be conveyed to the Highlands Ranch Metropolitan District.

background.text: The site was first platted for a different project. A 2023 submittal (referrals sent 2023-06-16) proposed 240 market apartments in two buildings, called "Kaos Apartments" in the drainage report. The 2026 plat staff report says the plan is now 165 units in a single building.

No rezoning was needed. PA 79 of the Highlands Ranch PD (approved 1979) allows multifamily for sale or lease by right. The County approval was a Minor Development Final Plat creating one 9.69-acre lot; news reports called it a "zoning request".

The Planning Commission heard the plat on 2026-03-02, and the Board adopted it on 2026-03-10 with four conditions: a burrowing owl study for earthwork between Mar 15 and Oct 31, watching for cultural resources, technical plat corrections, and applicant commitments made at the hearing. No public comments were received.

The County found no school, park or fee dedications due (already met within the Highlands Ranch PD) and required no Subdivision Improvements Agreement. Improvements will be secured with the site improvement plan.
Site improvement plan SP2026-027, "165 senior affordable apartments" on Lot 1, was submitted on 2026-04-21. The County listed the plat as completed on 2026-04-27.

Park deal: HRMD applied for a Location and Extent (LE2026-010) for "Kaos Park", an approximately 1-acre community park on Lot 1 with a community garden, fitness station, bocce, lawn, pavilion and 24 parking spaces. It will be built alongside the apartments and conveyed to HRMD. The Planning Commission hearing was 2026-08-17, and the County listed the L&E as completed on 2026-08-20.

Bond approval: DCHP held its Section 147(f) public hearing on 2026-09-11, after notice on 2026-09-04. On 2026-09-22 the Board adopted Resolution R-026-070 approving up to $37,000,000 of DCHP bonds for the roughly 165-unit 55+ project.
Bond cap: on 2026-03-24 the Board assigned all of the County's 2026 private activity bond cap ($14,247,633) to DCHP (Resolution R-026-020).

Affordability: Shea said the project follows its standard 4% LIHTC program, restricted to 60% AMI and age 55+. The length of the LIHTC extended-use covenant is not stated in the public records checked.

Shea Properties' track record nearby: The Audrey, a roughly 134-unit senior affordable building at 9350 Dorchester Street in Highlands Ranch, was also financed with DCHP bonds ($20,750,000 Multifamily Housing Revenue Note, Series 2020). Shea said The Audrey's waiting list is driving demand for The Gregory.

What 60% AMI means in Douglas County (CHFA 2026 limits): maximum rent $1,620 for a 1BR and $1,944 for a 2BR, including utility allowance; income limits $60,480 for 1 person and $69,120 for 2 people. Actual rents are not public.

discrepancies.text: Bond amount: CHFA's award report lists $29,900,000 of PAB; the County's 2026-09-22 public approval is for up to $37,000,000. The County figure is a not-to-exceed ceiling.

Unit count: the 2026-05-12 County Manager Report describes the completed plat as "concurrent SIP for 240 units"; the plat staff report and the SIP listing in the 2026-04-28 County Manager Report say 165 units. The 240 figure is the superseded 2023 two-building plan.
Lot size: 9.69 acres (plat staff report), 9.686 acres (L&E exhibit), 9.68 acres (County planning lists) and 9.86 acres (Redland's L&E narrative).
Park size: about 1 acre of improvements (County L&E staff report) versus about 1.9 acres the Highlands Ranch Herald reported Shea would allocate to the Metro District.
Type of approval: news reports call the 2026-03-10 action a "zoning request"; County records show a Minor Development Final Plat on land already zoned for multifamily.

60% AMI limits: the Denver Gazette quotes a 1BR maximum rent of $1,576 and a 1-person income limit of $58,860; CHFA's 2026 limits (effective 2026-05-01) are $1,620 and $60,480. The Gazette apparently used the prior year's table (inferred).

Owner name: the plat staff report names the applicant "Central Park at Highlands Ranch, LLC"; Redland's L&E narrative lists the owner/developer as "Central Park Retail at Highlands Ranch LLC"; the L&E staff report calls Shea Properties the current owner.

open_questions: Total development cost, equity investor and credit price, bond purchaser or lender, and permanent loan terms are not public.
Whose bond cap backs the $29.9M (DCHP's pooled County/Parker/Castle Rock cap across years, or a CHFA statewide share) is not stated.
Whether the land is contributed, sold or leased to The Gregory, LLC, and at what price, is not public; the land is privately owned by a Shea-related entity.
Whether DCHP takes an ownership role that would bring a property tax exemption is not stated in County records (inferred possibility only).
Rents, utility allowances, length of the affordability covenant, general contractor and architect are not public.
SIP SP2026-027 approval, building permit and bond closing dates are not yet public.
The Highlands Ranch Metro District's own project page for the Plaza Drive park (agreement terms, cost cap) blocked automated access (HTTP 403), so it is not cited.
